title: Integrated pricing launch runbook and release notes coordination
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Purpose: Create an operational runbook to coordinate the rollout of the new SKU and limits model, own the release notes and billing communications content, and sequence cross-team GTM tasks so customers and sales have a smooth migration path. This ticket aggregates the launch checklist, release-note drafts, stakeholder assignments, and gating criteria. It is the single source of truth for launch ops and external comms until GA.
acceptance_criteria: All public-facing release notes including SKU migration instructions are drafted and reviewed by Legal, Billing, and Support
Billing system test matrix (billing sandbox) shows parity for sample migrated accounts across 3 tiers
Sales enablement materials (one-pager, FAQ, migration script) are approved and uploaded to Drive
Rollout runbook with rollback steps and SLO guardrails is reviewed by Eng and SRE
Customer migration flow documented and validated with 2 pilot accounts
checklist: Draft public release notes (initial) — owner: PM
Coordinate legal review of pricing language — owner: Legal (via PM)
Create billing comms for invoices and post-change notices — owner: Finance/Billing Ops
Prepare support KB articles with step-by-step migration guidance — owner: Support
Build sales enablement pack: slide deck, migration scripts, objection handling — owner: RevOps
Run billing sandbox tests for SKU mapping and quota enforcement — owner: ENG Billing Team
Validate usage metering against new SKU tiers for 3 representative accounts — owner: Metrics/Observability
Finalize release notes and schedule with Docs and Marketing — owner: PM
Publish feature flag/rollout plan and canary targeting in Console — owner: Eng
Schedule cross-functional launch dry run with Engineering, Support, Sales, Legal — owner: PM
release_notes_draft:
Release title: Clearer SKUs and tiered limits to optimize cost and predictability
Summary: Today we are introducing a simplified SKU model and revised per-tier limits to make pricing more predictable and to reduce token costs for common inference patterns. The change affects how usage is categorized on invoices and introduces an automatic mapping for existing accounts.
What changes for customers:
- New SKU structure (Compute, Storage, Priority) replaces previous mixed unit billing
- Per-route and per-model limits are consolidated into tiered quotas. Check the KB for your account mapping.
Migration and billing impact:
- Existing customers will be automatically mapped to the nearest SKU/tier based on trailing 30-day usage. Audit your sample invoice in the Billing Sandbox.
- No immediate change to credits for customers on active promotions; promotions will be honored during the migration window.
Where to get help:
- Support: support@redwood.ai (use subject: Pricing Migration)
- Docs: /docs/pricing-migration
Planned rollout: staged canary for 10% of active accounts starting 2025-04-05, ramp to 100% by 2025-04-12 if all SLOs hold.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry run with internal accounts and pilot customers (2025-03-25 to 2025-03-31). Phase 1: Canary 10% accounts with monitoring and priority support (2025-04-05). Phase 2: Expand to 50% after 48h of stable metrics. Phase 3: Full rollout and final invoice reconciliation (target 2025-04-12). Rollback condition: sustained billing errors >0.5% of canary accounts or any critical revenue-impacting discrepancy.
communication_timeline: 2025-03-12: Initial stakeholder kickoff and PRD review
2025-03-28: Draft release notes shared with Legal and Support
2025-03-31: Dry run complete; results posted to Drive
2025-04-01: Final release notes approved and scheduled
2025-04-04: Customer advisory email scheduled (for canary customers)
risks: Customer confusion about SKU semantics leading to Support surge
Edge cases for accounts with atypical burst patterns mapping to wrong tier
Regulatory or contractual obligations for enterprise customers requiring opt-in
mitigation_actions: Pre-rollout validation: run synthetic traffic profiles against billing sandbox
Support playbook: prepare canned responses and escalation paths
Enterprise opt-out: flag to exclude named contracts from automatic migration
Close monitoring: 1-hour alerting window for billing anomalies during canary
pilot_results_summary: Pilot run with 2 mid-market customers and 1 enterprise test account showed expected mapping and no invoice delta above 0.2% after rounding. Support ticket volume was within normal bounds during the pilot. Two follow-ups: clarify wording in FAQ on burst billing, and add one more test for GPU-heavy inference patterns.
follow_ups: Add FAQ entry for 'burst vs sustained usage' and confirm final language with Legal
Schedule workshop with Sales on 2025-03-22 to rehearse migration conversations
Create quick checklist for AE to confirm before migrating a customer (billing sandbox snapshot)
notes: Meeting 2025-03-05: Agreement to automate migration with opt-out for legacy enterprise contracts. Agreed SLA for billing correctness during migration: 99.9% accuracy for canary. PM to own final customer advisory copy; Marketing to own send cadence.
